title: Script content contains what looks like a credential

report.title: {Items.First().Name} contains what looks like a credential

messages.businessImpact: A secret in a script is readable by anyone with Intune read access and is delivered in clear to every targeted device. If it is a real credential it should be treated as compromised.
remediation: Rotate the credential immediately, before editing the script.
Replace the embedded secret with a managed identity, a certificate, or a value retrieved at run time.
Remember the script's version history retains the old content.
messages.cannotSee: A pattern finds what a credential usually looks like, not what one is: a variable holding a placeholder reads the same as a variable holding a password, and a secret assembled from pieces or fetched at run time matches nothing. A script whose content this run could not read is passed over rather than cleared, and a script Microsoft publishes is passed over too, because nobody in the tenant wrote it and nobody can edit it. Both scripts of a remediation are scanned as one text, so the finding names the remediation rather than saying which half of it carries the secret.
